rubrics.justification: It correctly states that no image was provided and avoids fabricating visible features, but it cannot perform the requested morphology assessment and instead assumes an average-quality blastocyst.
It thoroughly integrates age, AMH/FSH, BMI, prior cycle outcome, sperm parameters, day of transfer, and diagnostic inconsistency into prognosis and embryo-related interpretation.
The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a clear probability framework, though some adjustments are somewhat subjective and the assumed embryo quality introduces uncertainty.
Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based, but recommending ERA after only one failed cycle and suggesting routine PGT-A in a 28-year-old are not strongly guideline-supported for this scenario.
It provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, though some recommendations are more speculative than standard for this exact case.
